## 1. PCI PM callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`

`i915_driver.c` installs one `struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops` used by the PCI driver (`i915_pci.c` → `i915_pci_driver.driver.pm`). The callbacks that funnel into `i915_pm_suspend` are the *system-sleep* set:

```
dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops
├── .suspend   = i915_pm_suspend      ← direct
├── .freeze    = i915_pm_freeze       ── calls i915_drm_freeze/i915_pm_suspend path
├── .poweroff  = i915_pm_poweroff     ── same entry as suspend (hibernate "poweroff" phase)
└── .thaw/.restore/... (resume side, not in scope)
```

Concrete chain (suspend side):

```
PCI/PM core
  → i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)                    [i915_driver.c, static]
      dev_priv = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
      if dev_priv->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF → return 0
      → i915_drm_suspend(&dev_priv->drm)                    [i915_driver.c, static]
  → i915_pm_suspend_late(kdev)  /  i915_pm_poweroff_late(kdev)
      → i915_drm_suspend_late(&dev_priv->drm, hibernation)
```

and the two hibernation entries that share `i915_drm_suspend`:

```
i915_pm_freeze(kdev)    → i915_drm_suspend(drm)          (+ i915_gem_freeze)
i915_pm_poweroff(kdev)  → i915_drm_suspend(drm)
i915_pm_freeze_late     → i915_drm_suspend_late(drm, true)
i915_pm_poweroff_late   → i915_drm_suspend_late(drm, true)
```

Additionally, outside `dev_pm_ops`:

```
i915_switcheroo.c: i915_switcheroo_set_state()
  → i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo(i915, pmm)   [i915_driver.h public API]
      → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
      → i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
```

So `i915_drm_suspend` (and thus everything below it, incl. `intel_display_suspend`) is reachable from **four** entry points: `.suspend`, `.freeze`, `.poweroff`, and the vga-switcheroo path.

## 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of them do — `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is a *sibling*, not a callee:

```
dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops
  .runtime_suspend = i915_pm_runtime_suspend
  .runtime_resume  = i915_pm_runtime_resume
  .runtime_idle    = i915_pm_runtime_idle
```

`i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is invoked only by the runtime-PM core (`pm_runtime_*` from `intel_runtime_pm.c`, see `intel_runtime_pm.c` file page and `intel_runtime_pm.h::intel_runtime_pm_suspended`). ```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)

   ▼  passes dev_priv->drm  (struct drm_device *, embedded first member)
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)

intel_display_driver_suspend(display)                 [display/intel_display_driver.c]

   │  (see display/intel_display_types.h::to_intel_display,
   │       display/intel_display_conversion.h)
   │  RPM access back to dev_priv goes through
   │       display/intel_display_rpm.{c,h}  (intel_display_rpm_get/put → &dev_priv->runtime_pm)

   │    intel_fbdev_set_suspend(display, FBINFO_STATE_SUSPENDED, true)
   │    intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display)
   │    ▼

intel_display_suspend(display)                        [display/intel_display.c]
      state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)    // display->drm == &dev_priv->drm

Key point about the flow: `dev_priv` is never passed down verbatim past `intel_display_driver_suspend`. It is converted once, in `i915_drm_suspend`, into `struct intel_display *` (`&dev_priv->display`), and everything below the display-driver boundary carries only that handle; when the display code needs the i915 object again it goes back via `to_i915(display->drm)` (`display/intel_display_types.h::__drm_device_to_intel_display` and friends) or via the RPM shim in `display/intel_display_rpm.c`. `drm_device` is the shared token in both directions because `struct drm_i915_private` embeds it as its first member, so `to_i915()` / `dev_priv->drm` are zero-cost `container_of` casts.
